item.title: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.description: This is the current deletions thread.
item.content:encoded:
All Staff-enacted Deletions are carried out according to the Deletions Guide.

Summary deletions result for:

  • Articles with malicious intent
  • Pages that are clearly unfinished.
  • Attempts to "game" site procedure, such as re-posting a non-rewritten article in an attempt to get around downvotes.
  • Blatantly plagiarized material.
  • An article posted outside of the current range.

If an author attempts to self-delete their work and fails to do so properly, including either by blanking the page or renaming it, it will be deleted properly by Staff.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.description: Have you joined the site because you're an avid reader and are planning to vote, comment, or just lurk on the site? Interested in helping develop the Next Best Thing? Post your introduction here!
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.
  • Did you know our site has a night mode version? If you're interested in that (and a few other neat things!), check out our Usertools page.
  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

  • So you want to be a concept reviewer?
  • So you want to be a draft reviewer?
  • And of course, remember the Criticism Policy!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Go ahead and respond to other new members if you find that your interests overlap, and definitely ask for reading suggestions if there's a particular kind of SCP article or tale you enjoy reading. If you're looking to get started as a critiquer, feel free to mention the kind of material you particularly want to see more of on the wiki! You might even see some of our authors drop by here from time to time, if you mention you liked their work! :)

Welcome to the site!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.description: Not entirely sure what you want to do now that you've joined, or are planning on contributing in an unusual way? Post your introduction here!
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, new site members/artists/gamers/social media watchers/roleplayers/etc.!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Here's some places to talk to get you all started off, now that you've arrived:

  • Games and Hobbies forum: Just started playing a new game or are wondering if any other SCP site members play your favorite game? Alternatively, wondering if anyone else paints minifigures or goes to conventions? Jump into the conversations here.
  • Media Discussion forum: Have a cool video or news article that just screams of the paranormal? Talk about it and other such things here!
  • Fan Work forum: Have a cool drawing or want to see the work of some of the other artists here? Have an SCP-based mod or board game in the works? This is the place to discuss!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Have fun mingling with the other new arrivals and talking about your interests, hobbies, and plans for taking over the universe. You might also see some of our veteran users here from time to time, since you never know when someone might be looking for an artist or a voice actor or an idea-haver for the next big collaboration article or SCP project! Talk and be merry. :)

Welcome to the site!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.description: Have you joined the site because you want to write an SCP article or tale of your own, sometime now or in the future? Post your introduction here!
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, prospective site writers! It's good to see you here!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

First off, a couple standard things to keep in mind as you get started towards adding your voice to the Foundation universe:

  • Definitely read the How to Write an SCP Guide and the pages in the Guide Hub that are relevant to your ideas!
  • Make a sandbox page for your works in progress, reference notes, inspirational snippets, and more author things!
  • Get familiar with our three Writing Help Forums:
    • Questions Desk: For all your questions about the writing process!
    • Ideas and Brainstorming: For asking about concepts that you're thinking of writing up! This is an especially important step for first-time authors!
    • Drafts and Critiques: For reviews of your finished pieces, to see what edits need to be made to your work to make it ready for the mainlist!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Feel free to respond to other new members if you find that your writing interests and/or plans overlap. The SCP wiki is a collaborative writing community, after all! You might even see some of the longtime writers here drop by with comments now and then. :)

Welcome to the site!

item.title: The Candy Cane
item.description: Sounds a little corny but I had this idea since Thanksgiving so I decided to try it out.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror and History

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: The SCP I envisioned is a plastic candy cane filled with small M&M-like candies that have different outcomes to it. While one candy that was eaten will give a person something like a lost possession or make them feel happy another could have immense tragedy or have the person who ate it either die or vanish through a trans dimensional entry way or property while a small select few saying that they are speaking for the candy cane.

Central Narrative: The story is mainly about how the candies affected history and while they test the object it shows some form of sentience and claims to have caused some of the worst tragedies and triumphs in history and saying that they had been the first thing consumed and will be the last thing consumed by man.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is just an idea that I had and wanted to share. While some SCP’s are intriguing for their gruesome nature and such I think an SCP that is more based on luck and a way to solve some of the worlds greater mysteries and why certain things happened would be a intriguing idea.

Additional Notes: I just have a problem of answering a genre. However, I am pretty confident in this even with a hiccup in that department. I will except all the feedback I can get because this one I want to see through till the end and make this my first SCP entry.

item.title: SCP-5233
item.content:encoded:
Big big big thanks to my lovely reviewers in chat: Pratten, Savan, Calibri_Bold, Mars, chaucer345, and Karakatt for all your wonderful suggestions to better develop the backstory here!

Image source is here: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_earwig_(Forficula_auricularia)_on_thumb.jpg

Notes:
- All of Wiggy’s interview excerpt dialogue consists of words found in the Wikipedia article for Earwig: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earwig
- Why earwigs? 1. When I was in elementary school, my friends and I found a very large pincher bug on the playground and admired it. Some other kid picked it up and tore off its pincers to keep as a souvenir. That image has stuck with me for over a decade. I can’t smush earwigs anymore. Also last month I found one in a box at work the other day and I let him go outside and it reminded me of that incident. 2. Quoth Wikipedia, “Earwigs are among the few non-social insect species that show maternal care.” Pinchy pinch moms are good moms. There’s a lot of neat facts about earwigs.
- Why Arizona? During my background research, I found this: https://cals.arizona.edu/yavapai/anr/hort/byg/archive/earwig.html so I just went with Arizona.

Best wishes to everyone in this crazy year. To everyone who has the opportunity to nurture a life, no matter how small, and those who teach others to do the same, you are the hope of the world.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Drama

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is approximately from 6 to 15 feet tall, dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, and has its general appearance as a tall black figure that has devoid facial features, and no sign of hair, nose, eyes, has unchecked limitations, and numerous of anomalous abilities. In all of which, it is in foundation custody. The Foundation's goal was to prevent its anomalous abilities from attempting to cause out an event of containment breaches by accident. The containment procedure was to keep SCP-XXXX inside a 16 x 60 ft (about 3.7 x 5.5m) room constructed out of tungsten.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid entity dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, comprised of a white shirt, a black or red tie, black trousers, and black shoes. It measures 6 to 15 feet tall has a general appearance as a tall black figure. However, it is possible that this is not SCP-XXXX's true form and that it is an eldritch being that cannot comprehend whose proper form. Its face is pitch black, utterly devoid of facial features. Despite lacking facial features, SCP-XXXX can sense when its targets are near at all times, as it never hesitates and always sees the targets around it. SCP-XXXX has various anomalous abilities that the Foundation was to yet discovered. The ones learned so far are based on the logs of the incident, description, experiments, and interviewing logs of the Foundation, which are:

+ show block
– hide block
  • Teleportation.
  • Mind-affecting.
  • Memory adding, erasing, and inhibiting.
  • Causing instant death by making eye contact with a subject longer than three (3) seconds.
  • Extremely high superhuman attributes.
  • Causing out technological disruption upon technologies in random moments without wanting it to do so.
  • Able to sense how dangerous the ones it confronts are.
  • The ability to let it cause out phenomenons to become an omnipresent being that can warp space and time between locations, or possibly reality.
  • Strong regenerative healing factor.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an SCP with an unknown past and couldn't remember a lot of who it was before becoming a humanoid entity that has various extremely dangerous and powerful anomalous abilities.

Additional Notes: I couldn't figure it out. People said that my grammar was having problems, but I've fixed my grammar errors and even improved my SCP article. What am I really missing?


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: First Time Author looking for review
item.description: essentially a voodoo doll, but bear with me, there's a twist
item.content:encoded:
At first glance it might seem boring, my idea is essentially a voodoo doll, but bear with me, there's a twist that I think is unique enough to give this a chance. I've been reading SCPs for years and I've always wanted to write my own but I usually scrap them because I don't think they're good enough, so I'm really excited to share this :)

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: voodoo doll that when picked up, causes the subject to fly into rage against the last person to anger them, the voodoo doll will take on the appearance of that person, and the subject will use it to kill the victim by any means available. These people are now known as SCP-XXX-1(Subject) and -2(victim). When the victim is killed, the doll reverts to its original form and repairs all damage, the subject will then lose their memory of interacting with the doll. After event XXX-01, it is discovered that the doll has a cognitohazard effect that makes people want to use it.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: In an addendum, event XXX-01 is described, along with an interrogation log and security tape transcript, where a guard unknowingly uses the scp to kill his boss while patrolling the anomalous item vault the object was contained in. It is investigated and found that the SCP has developed a new property while in containment, the O5 council releases a statement acknowledging the threat posed by this and suggests the development of an Emergent Properties Research Division (EPRD), in order to study the possible ‘evolution’ of anomalous properties in contained SCPs. The SCP is reclassified from safe to euclid, and containment protocols are updated

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook here is the emergent properties idea. I don’t think I’ve ever read an article that mentions SCPs ‘evolving’ new anomalous properties, and I explain it in the article as an adaptation made by the SCP in order to affect people while still in containment. I think it’s just a cool new thing to add to the lore, as well as creating a new branch of the foundation in the EPRD

Additional Notes: As mentioned in the title, I am a first time writer, so all criticism is welcome. I’ve been reading SCPs for years so I think I have a grasp on how to write them, but we’ll see how this is received. I have the full article written in my sandbox if you’d like to just read it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Stalker (Looking for Green Light)
item.description: A SCP that is always around a present
item.content:encoded:
A SCP that is always around a present, first you just saw it once at work, now no matter where you are it is always there.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The idea is a SCP that slowly creeps into the victim's life. At first he’s a random face in the street, not unlike the hundreds of unknown faces you pass everyday. But over time he's just there more often, now he's at the commissary, at your favorite restaurant, and you swear you saw him through your front window. Wait was he that person you just saw out the corner of your eye? This process then repeats but quicker with hearing him everywhere and then even quicker with feeling his presence everywhere. After this it seems he's not only around you at all times, but now he's in your head. Every moment, every thought he's there.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP article will be told through a series of interviews and documents. The central story is a chronological story told by a series of interviews and other documents. It starts with a victim recounting his story as defined in the hook below, and then followed by his missing papers. This man is the first known victim of the SCP and causes the SCP foundation to launch an operation into the man's town to try and find the SCP (told through a OPORD). While they do find the SCP it escapes by unknown means but one of the SCP agents gets infected by the SCP and is put into quarantine. After a month in quarantine being a SCP scientist checking on the Agent is infected and the Agent seemingly disappeared. The infected scientist escapes to the original victim's town, the rest of the story is finding why the SCP is attracted to here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook will be an interview between a SCP Scientist and a SCP victim. In the interview the victim, clearly traumatized by what's happening to him, recounts his story of how the SCP is everywhere. It's basically the elevator pitch in more detail. I put a *rough* draft for this interview below if yall want to see how this will look in execution.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure if this is similar to any other SCP, please tell me if it is. Note the final step after the SCP is always present in the victim's mind is eventually the victim becomes the SCP, still the same person, but now that person is the SCP.

Hook Rough Draft

Rough draft, I know this doesn't follow SCP Interview Protocols, will fix it in actual.
“I don't know who he is, no, I can’t even tell what he is. Everytime I go out he’s there, he’s a waiter, a random face in a crowd, or even my own co-worker, but no matter what he’s always there. It just doesn't make sense, he can’t physically be everywhere, no it's definitely impossible, it's unnatural. How can a single man be everywhere? Even when I'm in the safety of my own home… What cruel joke do I mean by saying safety, I hear his goddamn voice there too! Whether i’m eating or sleeping, his voice is just there. At first it was just another random voice I heard at work, you know one of those hundreds of random background voices you hear every day, but then I started hearing it more and more. Now *sob*, now it's all I can hear, for the love of god I don’t want to hear that wretched thing anymore. Even now, I see it, I hear it, … my god, it's here, I can feel it. *addressing SCP Scientist* Why, why is it here, you told me I would be safe here, but it's here. I know it's here, I can feel it! *standing up*Come out demon, where are you hiding!! *falling to the floor* Please, please just leave me alone.”


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts, and be mindful of the wordcount limit noted in the required reading. ~Zyn

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog
item.description: I’m looking for a greenlight for my SCP article idea.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Dramatic, Lighthearted

Elevator Pitch: This SCP would be a SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. The dog is also able to control small flames. Other than that, the dog is a completely average dalmatian.

Central Narrative: The narrative of this SCP article would be the discovery of this animal’s anomalous properties, descriptions of various SAR missions the dog was used on, and how the dog came to be contained by the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dog was the mascot of a fire station until it’s owners discovered its anomalous properties. It was subsequently trained as a SAR dog until it was contained by the Foundation. Presumably, given this SCP’s ability, prior training, and the ease of containment/control, the Foundation could potentially utilize this SCP for its own SAR missions during small incidents (i.e. fires, earthquakes) or even in assistance with small-scale breaches.

Additional Notes: I’m open to any critiques or suggestions. My plan is to make this article fairly straightforward and short given that this is my first. I’ve volunteered with SAR work and SAR dogs in the past so I wouldn’t need to conduct too much research.

Elevator Pitch: We can see the researcher ask for a member of Gamer Against Weed to help him to contain SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: Ok, so basically, the SCP is a drug that makes all the people that sniff it is all good and all of that. The anomaly is that it can't be stopped and will have some kind of dependence over it even when all the traces of it are being wiped out. So there's a containment breach over the site that contains it and the foundation try all they can to contain SCP-XXXX. A scientist has this idea about cooperating with Gamer Against Weed because of their experience with the drug SCP. Of course, the chance of GAW having actually experience with the drugs SCP is really little but it's their only chance. So the researcher that has found the idea will communicate with GAW and try to cooperate with them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The originality of my idea is that we never actually get to have Gamer Against Weed to be more serious and actually be not the kind of Goi that is just here for the laughs. Of course, they will still be the classic version.

item.title: Malicious Magnet (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A floating, anomalous magnetic object
item.content:encoded:
A floating, anomalous magnetic object that works like a normal magnet, except it has the ability to cause as much harm to humans as possible.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Similar to a standard SCP article, having 4 additional addendums that show testing logs.

Elevator Pitch: A floating, inanimate, red metal object that exhibits an anomalous magnetic force. It will work as a normal magnet when presented with most metal objects. However, it will alter its magnetic force when humans are around, causing pain (due to altering blood flow) or even death to individuals with things like pacemakers or prosthetic replacements. It will also destroy any technology that comes close enough using this force.

Central Narrative: The SCP was originally found in a meteoroid crash site. The anomaly was originally reported to the foundation because of the death of 3 individuals investigating the meteorite. It was relatively difficult to retrieve because it had torn the body armor of the MTF sent to investigate, causing major injuries to the chest area. It was eventually retrieved aircraft, towing it to containment through a long-distance hook.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think this SCP has the potential for a lot of interesting testing and theorizing, and I don't think a sentient magnet concept has been done before.

Additional Notes: It is unknown if this SCP is sentient or not.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Retro-Causality and You
item.description: SCP Article: Anomalous book can change the past and present
item.content:encoded:
SCP Article: Anomalous book can change the past and present and no one knows anything has changed except the book itself. Interesting events are recorded inside, how much of our past has been changed?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights:
Yes

Page Type:
SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional):
The Tests(not in the idea critique) can be cross referenced with the statements from the SCP to uncover what happened.
Statements of |||||||||| is text that has been scratched out beyond recognition

Elevator Pitch:
Dealing with retro-causality and how to test an anomalous object that can change the past.

  • Testers have issues discovering how the SCP functions since it wipes peoples minds and rewrites history and records the instance of the change.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

  • Book was discovered to have been placed into SCP containment by someone who might have known the books anomalous properties.
  • Unfortunate Accident causes it to end up in the research department
  • Marion Wheeler discovers and returns the book back to containment.
  • Testing begins
  • Containment Breach by a D-Class individual using the book during a test.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

Containment Summary-
While within 5 meters of SCP-####. Do not speak or write any untrue statements. In an emergency you can talk in future tense but you must not make any statement about the past or present (specifically opinions or statements that are false or have the possibility of being false)

Description Summary:
The text of SCP-#### is a range of statements about our world. More recent statements have been able to be verified as true. So far, no statements have been verified as false.

-Statements of probable significant interest from SCP -####

  • Multiple Historic Statements
  • ██████ has brought this book into a securely contained location under the protection of an organization that is currently trying to prevent its abuse in the future.
  • The research department is right around the corner from this SCP
  • I found the bug in your computer
  • ██████ doesn't belong here, he is an idiot
  • You totally threw █████████ under the bus
  • I found the issue with the computer system

item.title: Alternate dimension where man-made flight is nearly impossible

item.content:encoded:
This dimension is almost exactly the same as ours, except humans cannot go above a certain height limit in the atmosphere without going insane or catatonic.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science Fiction, Religion

Page Layout: There will be a series of interviews, documenting what the alternate universe is like, followed by an addendum showing how certain historical events have changed due to airplanes not being in wide use, and a final addendum that reveals its a world where God has deemed that humans are not allowed to leave the planet.

Elevator Pitch: This is an alternate dimension where man-made flight is essentially impossible, due to a phenomenon that occurs above a certain altitude (current thinking is about 6km up) that makes piloting and generally thinking rationally impossible.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The story will show how the Foundations of both universes try to work together to discover the cause of the anomaly, as well as discover the differences in each other's histories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Much of the history of the 20th's century was shaped by the advent of air power. But what if air power was never a thing? Air craft carriers, strategic bombing, mail by air, even tourism would all completely change. This SCP will examine ways such a world might work.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea for a couple of years now, but I was never sure what to do with it. Recently, I remembered that there's a verse in the Quran that says:

"O assembly of jinns and men! If you have power to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass (them)! But you will never be able to pass them, except with authority (from Allah)!"

Essentially, the cause is that in our world, God has allowed humanity to leave the heavens and earth, but in SCP-X, God has not allowed this.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs (Edited and revised)

item.content:encoded:
A mysterious restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in 19XX. The building was then contained by the Foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch:

*Green Man's chefs are green faceless humanoids wearing a chef's attire.
*They are sentient and are capable of speech despite without having a mouth.
*No one knows where the kitchen is.
*They are friendly to humans and would love to talk with them.
*When being asked anything about their kitchen, they'll become agitated and reply with "no".

Central Narrative: In 19XX, a restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in Alaska. The customers said that they've never seen the kitchen nor any door leading to it.
The Foundation then secured the restaurant and sent in agents to order food and report back on what they were served. Or at least, what they think they were served.

+ show block
– hide block

An agent was able to find the kitchen. He was wandering around the restaurant and found a hallway. He went in and saw a door. But, as he was about to open the door, the agent experienced extreme paranoia and ran away. The agent said that he felt that there was a voice warning him not to come in. Every step he took closer to the door, the voice became louder.

More agents were sent into the restaurant to find the hallway. No one found it and they returned to the entrance of the restaurant. But, 2 agents weren't present. After a couple of minutes, one of the agents was found. He was shaking in fear. The agent was asked on what happened. He said that he and the other agent found the door. They both went in despite the voice telling them not to come in. What the agent saw was terrifying. The second agent was then stabbed by one of the chefs and the agent managed to run away. Just when the agent was about to say what was the terrifying thing he saw, a chef appeared and ran towards the agent. The chef started to repeatedly stab him while [REDACTED]. More chefs appeared and they became aggressive to the other agents. The chefs chased all of them out of the restaurant. After the team managed to exit the restaurant, a closed sign appeared outside the door. The sign read "CLOSED. We are making adjustments to give you the best service".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These entities can cook delicious food with unknown ingredients. The kitchen was never seen so it remains a mystery on how these entities make the food.

  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Epstein didn't kill himself
item.description: The surveillance footage from Epstein's cell is anti-memetic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional):

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.description: A cokehead decides to snort more than just cocaine...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I have no clue

Elevator Pitch:

  • A cokehead grows ashamed of himself one day and decided to smash a few of his video games. He gets the bright idea to snort the fragments and discovers that doing so gives him a signifcantly weaker version of the main character's powers/skills/abilities/etc.
  • Example: snorting Super Mario Bros lets him jump 18 feet in the air. The catch? He'll break his ankles when he lands.
+What the heck did I just write...?
-Uhh....

Central Narrative:

  • After spending much of his life disappointing his family, friends and divorced spouse, he goes on a downward spiral and then discovers his anomalous ability.
  • At first, he tries to do good.
  • He tries to help an old lady cross the road by snorting Super Mario Bros, picking her up and jumping across the street. It doesn't end well.
  • Then he snorts Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and gets the Master Sword. He attempts to stop a bank robbery. However, he has no formal sword training and ends up dropping it, firing the Master Sword energy beam and accidentally killing someone's dog. The robbers then kick his ass and leave.
  • He finally decides to go down the road of villainy instead.
  • He snorts a copy of Megaman and tries to rob a bank. He ends up burning his hand off because it turns out human flesh isn't made to rapid fire concentrated plasma shots.
  • The Foundation finally notices him and tries to contain him.
  • He snorts a copy of Grand Theft Auto and tries to steal a car.
  • Well, he steals a car, alright.
  • He can't drive and ends up crashing into a fire hydrant.
  • The Foundation catch up to him.
  • Turns out, he kept a secret weapon all him all along; it's a little glass vial filled with fragments of a copy of Persona 5. He snorts it, magically dons a really beat up, low quality edgy black trenchcoat that smells like it hasn't been washed since Persona 1's release date.
  • He tries to summon Arsene and all he gets is a floating top hat that fires a tiny glob of darkness. All it does it make the Foundation Agent sneeze.
  • He gets contained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Um. Well. He snorts things.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.description: You know that fly that always seems to sneak its way into your room at night? Well, it can be much, much worse.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

Additional Notes: When the man goes to the edges of the city large tremors happen around him. It is unknown if him leaving will result in his neutralization. To counteract this he is forced by the foundation to stay in the inner area of the city until more information is found.

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Romance, History

Elevator Pitch: A siren that travels the world's seas in search of someone to marry. She exposes people to auditory and visual memetic agents that will make the exposed person fall in love with her; this usually ends with the siren accidentally drowning the exposed person. Any accurate depiction of her also carries this effect. However, the memes will only work on people who identify as a woman: people who identify as male will have a violent reaction to memes. The memes aren't distributed by artistic interpretations of her.

She first appeared in 1882; she was less of a problem then because she mostly isolated herself in the middle of the Atlantic ocean, not aware of the outside world. However, with the rise of mass media and the internet, she became more of a problem to secrecy as she began patrolling closer to large population centers and started placing advertisements carrying memetic agents on the internet through anomalous and non-anomalous means.

Central Narrative: The foundation originally discovered the siren in 1882, but due to her remote location, the foundation maneuvered ships away from her position and kept her mostly uncontained. The disappearance of Natalie Wood is the first real sign that the Siren has taken more provocative actions to secure a bride. The foundation can get a hold of her and does some interviews:

  • The first goes in-depth about her history: Her familial line is dying off and she was forced into marriage. However, due to her sexuality and her failing relationship with her husband, she ran away from home in search of another bride.
  • The second has the foundation propose an alternative; she can find a bride within the foundation staff as long as she stops advertising on the internet.
  • The third is a list of multiple proposed brides, equipped with memetic dampeners, and the siren's reaction to them. One of them gets selected, and some conversations are logged. It ends on a sweet tone, the siren finally having found someone who likes her back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a wholesome article and this is mostly targeted at an audience that likes that, and it's pretty big. It also plays with the siren formula and introduces it to a modern setting. You could see it as a more family-friendly version of the original ''teenage succubus'' SCP.

item.title: SCP: Kingdom Come my first tale
item.description: The book of revelations with SCPs, inspired by DC's Kingdom Come
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi,

I'm planning on writing a meta SCP article on the McCollough effect. Thing is, I suppose you could say this is a real-life cognitohazard. Viewing the images can alter the way your brain perceives colour, causing long-lasting changes to colour perception. In some cases, the effects have lasted months after initial viewing.

I could totally do this… there are McCollough images that are CC compliant. Thing is, this could affect people in real life. I guess I would need some sort of disclaimer warning the reader of the image, but people are just going to assume the warning is fictional. It's not, and these images can alter you in real life.

I don't know how to write a disclaimer that will properly inform the reader of the potential repercussions whilst not breaking the tone of the site.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.description: an SCP article about a mysterious shadow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

The entity that replies through the paper is hyperintelligent, having knowledge of the O5 council and Level 5 clearance information that's withheld even from the researchers working on the SCP. It also has the ability to force anyone to grant any request that they read, which leads to many attempted escapes.

Central Narrative: A pair of entities, a pen and piece of paper, is discovered within an undisclosed SCP Site storage closet. After a junior researcher attempts to use the pen and paper together, he turns it in to his higher-ups, who begin experimentation on the entity. After discovering it's many abilities, such as it's incredible knowledge and it's way of making peopel complete requests, it is given strict safety and testing measures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The way that the paper is very knowledagble about the Foundation, and how it can make people grant it's requests. It's a mysterious entity that much isn't known about, which leads to myriad tests on said entity.

Additional Notes: Looking especially for critique on how it makes people fufill the requests of readers, or if there's something that could work better with the idea.
